sources.entry: Hazel - Automated file organization for your Mac. Responsibly and beautifully designed.

summary.name: Hazel
summary.one_liner: Hazel is a Mac app that watches chosen folders and automatically moves, renames, tags, archives or deletes files according to rules you create.
use_cases: keep the desktop free of clutter
empty trash when it gets too big or files get old
find and remove leftover app support files after uninstalling
summary.what_it_does: Hazel monitors whichever folders the user specifies and applies user-created rules to files in them. Rules can act on attributes such as name, date, type, and the site a file came from. Actions include moving, renaming, sorting into subfolders, opening, archiving, tagging, and uploading. It supports pattern matching to combine attributes into workflows. It can also clean the trash by deleting old files or emptying it when it grows large. Its App Sweep feature detects when an application is moved to the trash and offers to remove its leftover support files.
notable: App Sweep finds and offers to remove support files left by deleted apps
Rules can match on name, date, type, source site, and combined attributes
Can watch multiple user-chosen folders continuously
caveats: Mac-only: the page names macOS as the platform
Pricing is not stated on the page
